items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1960-01-21
items.q: Charlie used to play with me. But he never did own a band. He used to play with John Robeshoe's band. And that's why I was playing with him.

ctx.x: Did he, ask him, did he hear the Pillars?

Charlie McCurdy? Wait, let me see. George McCurdy's the man, huh? Yeah. Now, Charlie? Did he play? Soft. Soft. So he played soft. Oh, Charlie, yeah. Charlie used to play with me. But he never did own a band. He used to play with John Robeshoe's band. And that's why I was playing with him. And then from there, Louis the man got him. But he was so soft. After he got off the clarinet, he got on sack. And we thought by him getting on sack, he would blow loud, but it was the same thing. He did kick in, but he was a…
Well, I asked him, did he hear the Peerless band?

items.title: Clarence "Little Dad" Vincent Interview, 1959-12-03
items.q: Oh, but if he played soft, we, we could hear him.

ctx.x: Who was the guitar player before you?

Yeah. Who was the guitar player with Robichaux before you? Um, Kitcher Martin. You know what I'm talking about? And his brother was playing drums, you know. Uh, but his brother wasn't playing drums, Kitcher Martin was playing with Rose, but he had to leave Kitcher Martin to lose, and Timman, Henry Timman, let him lose, and, uh, ! Yeah, Tyler McCurdy. Yeah, Tyler McCurdy. And he was, he was a professor, Tyler, and he could play, but he couldn't hear him good. He's soft. He couldn't blow loud. Yeah. Never talked,…
Well, who was the next clarinet player after, could you, after Charlie McCurdy?
